title: Producer Agreement: Non-Exclusive Beat Lease
summary: License a beat non-exclusively for one song, with stream, sales and video caps. The producer keeps ownership and can lease the beat to others.
useWhen: An artist buys a lease on a beat from a producer or beat store and records one song over it.
watchOuts: Non-exclusive means other artists may use the same beat. If the song takes off, the artist may need to upgrade, and the beat may already be licensed elsewhere.
Know the caps. Once streams, sales or video views pass them, the artist must upgrade or stop. Distributors can take songs down over unlicensed beats.
Content ID: the artist should not register the beat, or the song, in YouTube Content ID or similar systems, because that will flag other licensees and the producer.
Sync (film, TV, ads, games) is usually not included. Get a separate sync license.
Writer splits on the new song should be documented in a split sheet. Leases commonly give the producer 50% of the composition, but that is negotiable.
If the beat contains an uncleared sample, every licensee inherits the problem. Ask in writing.

variables.label: New song title
variables.help: Title of the artist's song using the beat, if known.

variables.label: License term (years)
variables.help: How long the license lasts. Many leases are 1 to 5 years, some perpetual.

variables.label: Live performance allowed?
variables.help: For-profit live performances of the New Song.

variables.label: Price to upgrade to an exclusive license
variables.help: Optional upgrade price, credited by the lease fee if stated.

variables.label: Producer's share of the new composition
variables.help: Producer's writer and publishing share of the new song (the music). The artist and other writers share the rest. Register it with your PROs and The MLC.

variables.label: Producer credit
variables.help: How the producer is credited in titles and metadata.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 1. Parties
2. License
sections.body: On payment of {{fee}}, Producer grants Artist a non-exclusive, worldwide license to record one New Song using the Beat, and to reproduce, distribute, stream and publicly perform that recording within the limits below, for {{term_years}} years from the date above. Producer delivers the Beat as {{files}}.

sections.title: 3. Limits
4. Live performance
sections.body: Artist may perform the New Song live, including at for-profit shows. Venue public-performance licensing is handled by the venues and PROs.

sections.title: 5. Radio
sections.body: Artist may permit radio broadcasts of the New Song.

sections.title: 6. Not included
sections.body: Not included without a separate written license: synchronization with film, TV, ads, games or trailers; use of the Beat for more than one song; selling, leasing or giving away the Beat on its own; and registering the Beat or New Song in YouTube Content ID or any similar fingerprinting system. Artist: [[initial:artist]]

sections.title: 7. Ownership
sections.body: Producer keeps all ownership of the Beat, including its composition and sound recording, and may continue to license it to others. Artist owns Artist's lyrics, vocals and other original contributions, and the New Song master recording, subject to this license and Producer's rights in the Beat.

sections.title: 8. Composition and publishing
sections.body: The New Song's composition will be co-owned. Producer owns {{producer_share}}% (as writer of the music, including the corresponding publisher share), and Artist and any other writers own the rest, as recorded in a split sheet signed by all writers. Producer's PRO and IPI: {{producer_pro}}. Each party registers its own share with its PRO and The MLC. Neither party may register the New Song with a different split.

sections.title: 9. Credit
sections.body: Artist will credit Producer as "{{credit}}" in the song title or description where customary (for example "prod. by"), in streaming and distributor metadata where available, and in physical or digital liner notes. Inadvertent failure to credit is not a breach if Artist fixes it promptly after notice.

sections.title: 10. Upgrade
sections.body: Artist may upgrade to an exclusive license at any time while the Beat is still available, for {{upgrade_price}}, with the lease fee credited toward it. Upgrading does not cancel licenses Producer granted to others before the upgrade.

sections.title: 11. Producer's promises
sections.body: Producer promises that its contribution is original, or that every sample, interpolation or third-party element in it has been disclosed in writing and is either cleared or will be cleared before release. Producer has not granted rights that conflict with this agreement. Producer owns or controls the Beat and has the right to grant this license.

sections.title: 12. Artist's promises
sections.body: Artist's lyrics, vocals and other contributions are original or cleared, and will not infringe anyone's rights or be defamatory.

sections.title: 13. Ending the license
sections.body: If Artist materially breaches this agreement, for example by exceeding the limits without upgrading, and does not cure within 15 days after written notice, the license ends and Artist must remove the New Song from distribution. The fee is non-refundable once the files are delivered.

sections.title: 14. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Producer** — {{producer_name}}

[[sig:producer]]

Printed name: [[name:producer]]
Date: [[date:producer]]

**Artist** — {{artist_name}}

[[sig:artist]]

Printed name: [[name:artist]]
Date: [[date:artist]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
